current.text: He re-signed with Sacramento for 2 years and 11.5 million USD.
He is projected as a bench big behind starter Domantas Sabonis.
Dylan Cardwell (calf strain) and Maxime Raynaud are both out at least two weeks to start the season. Achiuwa and a two-way big get the backup center minutes.
The Kings may also play small ball with Ben Simmons at center, which can take backup center minutes.
His strong late-season stretch came while Sabonis, Keegan Murray, DeAndre Hunter and Cardwell were out. All of them are back.
Do not draft him off his late-season run. Experts say his post-deadline rank was not real and that an ESPN rank of 111 was too high.
He is a short-term target in deep leagues only, as the backup center while Cardwell and Raynaud are out.
Yahoo lists him as questionable with an ankle injury.
Experts call the Kings one of the worst teams in the NBA, with poor coaching and front office, which makes their rotations hard to predict.
The Kings play 4-4-3 games in our playoff weeks 19 to 21, 11 games in total. They have 14 back-to-backs this season.

durable.text: His fantasy value comes from rebounds and FG%. His free throw shooting is poor, but on low volume.
He makes very few threes and adds few points or assists.

note: Do not draft him. Both Yahoo and ESPN value him at 0 USD (Yahoo rank 201, ESPN rank 153), and he went undrafted in our league last season, so he is well outside our 144-player pool. In the first weeks, watch the waiver wire: if his ankle is fine and he gets steady backup center minutes while Cardwell and Raynaud are out, he can be a short-term streamer for rebounds and FG%. His FT% is poor but on low volume. Drop him once both are back.
